  Readable gloss: "Yishai (Jesse) is the father of David and grandson of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22), anchoring the royal line in the story of Moabite redemption. His name appears 42 times, predominantly in 1 Samuel 16-17 where Samuel is sent to anoint a king from his house. The patronymic ben-Yishai ('son of Jesse') becomes a loaded political designation: Saul uses it dismissively (1 Sam 20:27, 30; 22:7-8), and Sheba's rebel cry 'we have no portion in the son of Jesse' (2 Sam 20:1) echoes into the northern secession. Isaiah's 'shoot from the stump of Jesse' (11:1, 10) transformed the name into a messianic symbol."

Functions as narrative identifier (1 Sam 16:1-3) and politically charged patronymic — Saul's dismissive 'son of Jesse' (1 Sam 22:7-8) contrasts with the messianic 'root of Jesse' (Isa 11:10).
    Existing Spanish translations: Yishai, a-Yishai
